ticks.note: Tick 1 enters `ABO`, then `WaitAB`, then `WaitA` and `WaitB`, all at once. Every transition is delayed, so this tick only sets things up.
`B` arrives first this time: `HandleB` finishes in `DoneB`. The order of `A` and `B` does not matter.
Nothing present. `DoneB` remembers that `B` has happened.
`A`: `HandleA` finishes too. Both regions are final, so the `join to` fires in this tick and emits `O`.
`O` is a signal, so it is absent again: it was present in exactly one tick. `ABO` now rests in `Done`.
`A` and `B` are ignored: `Done` waits for `R`, nothing else.
`R`: the strong abort `if R abort to ABO` leaves `ABO` and enters it again from its initial states. `WaitAB` starts over in `WaitA` and `WaitB`.
`A` and `B` in the same tick: both regions finish in this tick, so `WaitAB` terminates and `O` is emitted at once.
All three at once. `R` wins: `ABO` is re-entered, and the re-entered `WaitA` and `WaitB` cannot react to `A` and `B` in their entry tick (their transitions are delayed). `O` is absent.
The `A` and `B` of the last tick are not remembered: ABRO waits for a fresh `A` and `B`.
